summary: Black Drift duel: Abby answers a rival captain without a speech.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT HAVEN — OPEN SALVAGE GANTRY — NIGHT

dialogueInline.speaker: Rival Captain
dialogueInline.text: You don't give orders on my deck.

directionInline: Open on the salvage gantry with crews ringed around a practical dispute that has already turned physical. The rival captain blocks Abby's path and says the first line. Abby answers while stepping inside his reach, strips the weapon in one ugly motion, and dumps him into the netted salvage pit. Final image: Abby keeps walking toward the waiting ships while somebody hauls him out; she never turns the victory into a speech.

summary: Abby's war deck: survival doctrine collides with Billie's appetite for spectacle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: And if a farm takes a shot at me?

directionInline: At the engine-cowling map table, Abby physically removes Billie's marker from the farm settlements and drops it on the feeder route. Billie puts it back with one finger; Abby moves it again. Tess watches from the edge of the table. The conversation plays over that small contest, so the raid boundary is visible before anyone explains it.

summary: The Silent Triarch reduces a war to three brutal verbs.
directionInline: Treat this as ritual, not ordinary conversation. Three masks sit above the captains; each gives one formal line and nothing else. Abby receives the decree standing, arms at her sides, and does not bow. The long silent reaction after the third line is the point of the scene.

summary: At Auric Bazaar, policy sounds different when spoken beside people who need heat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: North Ring has heat for two nights. Clinic's down to six antibiotic trays.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: And the Fleet wants half our docking revenue for escorts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The cheap route lost three ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: The third one is six hours late.

directionInline: Halev walks the market while talking, checking a heater repair queue and a clinic manifest rather than giving a speech from a table. Wallace keeps pace with the account slate. Naomi arrives from the docks and corrects him without slowing down. The failed heater core and clinic queue make the stakes visible.

summary: Halev chooses the green corridor because every alternative is worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Wallace
dialogueInline.text: You're really going to let the Fleet set the route?

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: For one night, I'm going to let whoever gets the food here set the route.

directionInline: Halev stops beside a parent trying to restart a failed heater module while the clinic line advances under weak light. Wallace is still arguing from the slate. Halev looks from the family to the dark apartment ring beyond the canopy and makes the decision there, then points toward the docks.

summary: The Admiralty argues whether a humanitarian lane is mercy or an exposed throat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: Open one lane and they'll use it to measure the wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: Keating
dialogueInline.text: And when the first freighter brings rifles?

directionInline: The route glows between the admirals on the council table. Dominion closes the projected corridor with two fingers as he speaks. Venn reopens only one narrow lane. Keating brings up a weapons-scan image; Rhyne answers while enlarging the civilian cargo numbers beside it. Nobody addresses the reader; they are arguing over the same live map.
panelPlan: Wide: Dominion above the council table; the proposed green lane glows inside the blockade.
Dominion closes the lane on the map. Venn reaches in and restores one narrow route.
Keating throws a weapons-scan image beside the route; Venn watches her, not the display.
Rhyne taps the civilian cargo totals. Dominion turns on him for the final exchange.

summary: Dominion permits the experiment without conceding the principle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Dominion
dialogueInline.text: One lane. One window. You lose it, I close it.

directionInline: Dominion leaves the single green route active and kills every other proposed window. Venn studies the one remaining line, gives him a short acknowledgment, and turns for the door before he can make the concession feel generous.

summary: The Shards swear their war-moot with engines instead of words.
settingText: BLACK DRIFT HAVEN — EXTERIOR SALVAGE DECK — NIGHT
directionInline: Let the engines do the talking. Shard ships ring Black Drift; captains climb into mismatched hulls, deck crews pull away umbilicals, and one engine after another lights until the haven becomes a rough constellation. Abby watches the departures from the gantry. Tess catches her eye from Gravefire before sealing her hatch. No voice-over.

summary: The feint begins: Billie treats Abby's restraint as an insult and enters wanting destruction rather than leverage.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Lead ship's fat with machine parts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: And wearing enough armor to advertise them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Abby marked a feint. I'm looking for a wound.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: There you are. Shift the solution.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: That takes us out of line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Only if you plan on coming back.

directionInline: Ashfang enters in Abby's disciplined skiff line, but Billie is already refusing the premise of a feint. A raider offers the valuable lead ship and invokes Abby's mark. Billie searches instead for pain she can exploit, finds the third freighter sagging under engine trouble, and makes her crew choose between formation and her appetite. The scene turns when the targeting solution moves; Ashfang leaves the line before it fires.
panelPlan: Wide: the civilian convoy threads a damaged feeder truss while Abby's pale-gray skiffs hold a precise attack line.
In Ashfang's industrial-black cockpit, a raider offers the armored lead ship. Billie dismisses the obvious prize and scans the formation for weakness.
The raider invokes Abby's mark. Billie finds the third freighter riding low with a stressed engine plume and calls it a wound.
Billie orders the solution shifted. The raider warns that the move breaks formation; Billie answers without looking away from the target.
Exterior consequence: the other skiffs preserve Abby's spacing while Ashfang noses out of line, red targeting light settling over the vulnerable third freighter.

summary: Venn refuses the bait and chooses civilian protection while her officers expect retaliation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Third freighter is falling back. I have pursuit solutions.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Commodore, they expect us to chase.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: If we don't, they keep the initiative.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: They can have it. Stay with the freighters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Make us difficult to shoot around.

directionInline: The bridge presents Venn with the satisfying military answer: three clean pursuit solutions. She refuses to discuss the raiders until she knows which civilian ship is failing. Her officer presses the cost—ceding initiative—and Venn knowingly pays it. She cancels the attack geometry and makes Thunderbreak a moving wall beside the freighters. The bridge must feel the choice, not merely execute an order.
panelPlan: Bright Fleet bridge: red pursuit solutions bloom around three skiffs while a tan-green freighter drops behind the convoy.
The officer reports the attack and offers pursuit. Venn asks about the convoy instead; the failing third ship is isolated on the display.
Venn removes the pursuit vectors. The officer warns that this gives the raiders the initiative; Venn accepts the cost.
She drags Thunderbreak's blue course alongside the civilian icons and orders the ship made difficult to shoot around.
Wide exterior payoff: Thunderbreak settles beside the patched freighters as a moving wall while the skiffs retain open space—and lose their clean firing lanes.

summary: Tessa quietly saves lives while everyone else is looking for a fight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Freighter, cut your beacon. Drift with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Tethers caught. Billie is sweeping back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: Don't fight the spin. Let the wreckage hide us.

directionInline: A medpod freighter tumbles out of cover into Ashfang's search. Tess chooses rescue before asking permission, forcing her second to accept going dark under friendly guns. She talks the terrified freighter pilot through surrendering control while Gravefire catches the ship with micro-tethers. The firing cone passes over them because Tess lets both vessels spin into debris shadow. Her crew names the deviation; Tess makes it the mission.
panelPlan: A medpod freighter tumbles from the feeder structure, medical pods exposed through a ruptured cargo frame; Ashfang's search cone begins to turn toward it.
On Gravefire, Tess orders the beacon killed. Her second objects that nobody will see them; Tess launches micro-tethers anyway.
The tethers bite. Tess tells the freighter pilot to cut their beacon and stop fighting the spin as Gravefire rolls with the heavier ship.
Ashfang's firing cone sweeps across their dark cockpit. The second reports the danger; Tess uses the wreckage rather than thrusting away.
Wide: both ships settle into debris shadow. The second says this was not the raid; Tess answers, 'It is now,' while the crew keeps the rescued ship stable.

summary: Billie breaks the plan because destruction is the point for her.
directionInline: With the chosen freighter protected, Billie searches for a way to make restraint hurt. Her raider identifies the exposed storage spine but also names what the cargo means. That knowledge is not a deterrent for Billie; it is the reason she chooses the target. She overrides Abby's withdrawal and orders fire twice. The supplies erupt against dark habitat rings. Only afterward does the spectacle fail her: her crew looks at the unheated homes, and Billie cannot manufacture the grin she expected.
panelPlan: Ashfang shears from Abby's withdrawal vector as its raider reports the freighter protected behind Thunderbreak.
Billie retargets the exposed storage spine. The raider identifies heater cells and food and warns that the habitat rings need them.
Billie says 'Exactly' and orders fire. When the raider hesitates, she repeats the command face-to-face.
Dominant impact: heater cells, food tins, and thermal blankets erupt into a brilliant debris sheet before several dark civilian habitat rings.
Aftermath close: reflected fire crosses Billie and the silent raider. The cheer she wanted never comes; outside, the habitat windows remain dark.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Third freighter slipped behind the cruiser.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: She wanted their eyes. We have them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Storage spine is heat and food.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raider
dialogueInline.text: Those rings go cold without it.

summary: Thunderbreak physically blocks Billie's firing lane instead of escalating the battle.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Ashfang's lining up on the clinic ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tactical
dialogueInline.text: Not with weapons. Eight seconds late.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Shoulder through. Keep the clinic moving.

directionInline: Ashfang's firing cone closes on the clinic freighter. The tactical officer proves that a conventional intercept will arrive too late, so Venn asks for the dangerous physical alternative. She commits Thunderbreak to crossing the cone at close range and then accepts a broken feeder truss in the path. The cruiser shoulders through and takes the exposed position. Ashfang fires; Thunderbreak is scarred, but the clinic ship keeps moving.
panelPlan: The clinic freighter fills the tactical display as Ashfang's cone closes; the officer reports that a weapons intercept is eight seconds late.
Venn asks what the engines can do. The officer offers crossing the cone, then warns it puts Thunderbreak inside Ashfang's range.
Venn accepts. A broken truss appears in their path; she orders the cruiser to shoulder through and keep the clinic moving.
Large exterior: Thunderbreak smashes the feeder beam aside and crosses between Ashfang and the clinic ship.
Sparks rake Thunderbreak's armor as Ashfang fires. Behind the cruiser, the clinic freighter escapes the cone and continues toward safety.

summary: Naomi turns a frightened escort line into something that can hold.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Blue Two, you're drifting. Get back on me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Their port thruster's gone. Give them our line.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Blue Two, follow my burn. Don't correct—just follow.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Clinic pods inside the line. Come on.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: There you go. Close us up.

directionInline: Blue Two drifts out because a thruster has failed, not because its pilot lacks nerve. Naomi diagnoses it while frightened herself and chooses to expose her own escort for six seconds to give the crippled ship a course it can copy. Her second counts the danger down as Naomi talks Blue Two through one simple action. The formation closes around the clinic pods just before the exposure becomes fatal. Naomi's gentleness arrives only after the ship is safe.
panelPlan: Naomi's scratched display shows Blue Two breaking right and clinic pods slipping toward the opening; her second reports the drift.
Naomi gets no answer, spots the dead port thruster, and orders their own ship out to provide a flight line. Her second warns this exposes them to Ashfang.
Naomi commits to six seconds. Close on her trembling hand as she burns across the gap and tells Blue Two not to correct—only follow.
Exterior: Blue Two copies Naomi's burn while the second counts down and the clinic pods pass into the recovering arc.
The line closes. The second confirms Blue Two has it; Naomi allows herself 'There you go,' then orders the formation closed before Ashfang can exploit the move.

summary: Billie and Tessa leave the same raid with opposite lessons.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You tucked a freighter in my blind side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You made a very large blind side.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: I was. That's why they're alive.

directionInline: Ashfang and Gravefire cross on withdrawal, bringing Billie face-to-face with the freighter Tess stole from her firing cone. Billie claims the ship as prey; Tess insists on the people inside it. Their exchange sharpens until Billie turns the discovery into a future threat. Tess does not plead or moralize. She names the actual difference between them and leaves with the living freighter still under her protection.
panelPlan: Ashfang and Gravefire cross nose-to-tail amid feeder debris; Billie discovers the medpod freighter tucked in Gravefire's shadow.
Magnified cockpit feeds lock Billie and Tess together. Billie accuses Tess of using her blind side; Tess points out Billie created it.
Billie claims the ship. Tess answers with its patients; Billie's glib dismissal dies against Tess's blunt reply: 'Not after you.'
Billie warns Tess to be careful. Tess gestures to the intact freighter: she was, and that is why they are alive.
Billie promises not to miss next time. Tess answers 'Then look first' as the ships separate and Gravefire keeps the freighter covered.

summary: Jex sells Halev what institutions cannot quite provide: a compromise that can function now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I don't think we can get by with any less than eight ships.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: That's six more than you have now. I can give you four additional.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I said I need six from you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Do you know any other smugglers?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Fine. Five. I'm either getting weak or lazy. Dammit. Five.

directionInline: Halev needs eight ships and has only two. Jex offers four more and treats the remaining shortage as Halev's problem; Halev refuses the arithmetic and makes Jex own the human need behind it. Jex threatens to walk, then discovers Halev has no competing smuggler to call. The silence reverses the leverage just enough for Halev to win a fifth ship. Jex complains while adding it to the manifest, making the compromise real.
panelPlan: Wide office/docks: two available supply ships sit beyond the window; the manifest shows eight required. Halev states the minimum.
Jex taps the two existing hulls, adds four, and calls the remaining gap Halev's. Halev repeats that he needs six from Jex.
Jex leans back and suggests another smuggler. Halev does not chase the bluff or fill the silence.
Jex asks whether Halev knows another smuggler. Naomi watches from the window as both men recognize the answer.
Halev offers five—not gratitude, a number. Jex studies him, then accepts.
Jex physically adds the fifth ship, complaining that he is getting weak or lazy; the manifest now contains a corridor that can actually function.

summary: Naomi and Jex establish their relationship while Halev accepts a temporary authority he does not trust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: You want them inspected or on time? Pick the expensive one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: I want weapons off my docks.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Rapid scans. No holds unless somebody finds a weapon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: I admire how quickly she finds the invoice.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Disputes go to you. For now.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: He's going to make that his title.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Temporary means I can take it back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Then we'd better make it indispensable.

directionInline: With five ships secured, Naomi finds the clause that could turn the corridor into either a weapons route or an inspection trap. Jex frames safety and speed as a price choice; Halev and Naomi force both needs into one workable rule. Naomi then exposes the unresolved question of authority. Halev grants Jex temporary arbitration, and Jex stamps the title before the governor can soften it. Halev warns that the authority can be revoked; Jex reveals his intention to make that politically difficult.
panelPlan: At the same desk, Naomi takes the five-ship agreement and discovers there is no inspection rule. Jex makes speed sound like a commodity.
Halev insists on keeping weapons off his docks; Naomi adds that medicine cannot be stranded. Halev writes rapid scans with no holds absent a weapon.
Naomi asks who decides disputes. Jex already has his stamp under one hand and deflects with a joke about invoices.
Halev grants Jex arbitration 'for now.' Jex stamps the clause before Halev lifts the stylus; Naomi catches him making it a title.
Halev says temporary authority can be taken back. Jex answers that they should make it indispensable, leaving all three looking at the new power embedded in a practical agreement.

summary: The first corridor tests whether armed rivals can all choose not to fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Blue Three, ease left. You're crowding the batteries.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Thunderbreak is outside your lane. Weapons cold.

directionInline: The first five freighters enter carrying visible necessities. Naomi has to fly the convoy while negotiating armed presence on both sides. Venn confirms Thunderbreak will remain outside the lane; Naomi pointedly makes her repeat the restraint. Gravefire appears without clearance, and Tess refuses to offer more than an honest statement of intent. Naomi cannot make anyone trust anyone else. She chooses to continue anyway, and the armed ships let the convoy advance.
panelPlan: Five patched freighters enter the narrow green markers through fractured debris, with heater cores, medpods, batteries, and food visible in their cargo frames.
Naomi corrects Blue Three away from the batteries while her second reports Thunderbreak moving; Venn confirms the cruiser is outside the lane with weapons cold.
Naomi makes the restraint explicit. Venn answers that it is the order, not a favor.
Gravefire resolves at the far marker. Naomi challenges Tess's intent; Tess answers only 'Watching,' and tells Naomi to keep flying.
Wide across all forces: targeting brackets hover but do not lock. Naomi leads the freighters forward, turning mutual suspicion into the first functioning crossing.

summary: Billie tests the corridor and discovers Abby can still stop her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: One soft freighter and three armed witnesses pretending not to see it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You're really stopping me for this?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: It doesn't have to. Throttle down.

directionInline: Billie stalks the weakest freighter and assumes the corridor's restraint is cowardice she can exploit. Abby puts her own skiff across Ashfang's approach and orders Billie back. Billie tries mockery, grievance, and a demand for justification. Abby refuses to debate the corridor or expose the deeper change in her thinking; she makes obedience personal and immediate. Billie throttles down, but converts the humiliation into a debt she intends to collect.
panelPlan: Ashfang emerges behind the convoy, closing on its weakest freighter while Billie mocks the armed ships holding fire.
Abby's smaller skiff crosses the approach. She orders Billie to fall back; Billie greets the intervention like a performance she expected.
Canopy-to-canopy, Billie asks whether Abby is really stopping her for this. Abby answers, 'I'm stopping you for me.'
Billie demands that the answer make sense. Abby refuses the debate and orders the throttle down.
Billie pulls back but says Abby owes her a target. Abby's 'Get in line' lands as Ashfang returns behind the other skiffs rather than attacking.

summary: Jex runs the corridor from a back room and prepares to survive either outcome.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Marker Two is clean. Halev wants confirmation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Halev wants certainty. Confirmation is cheaper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Captain Oris wants his bribe back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: Then call it a corridor fee.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: If this works, it was my corridor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: I have your stamp on twelve authorizations.

directionInline: Jex runs the crossing through conflicting demands: Halev wants certainty, a captain wants money back, and every authorization bears Jex's exposure. His scribe keeps making him say what the paperwork means. Jex carefully distinguishes an open corridor from a safe one, renames a bribe as infrastructure, and assigns credit and blame to different futures. The scribe punctures his deniability by counting the stamped authorizations. Jex responds by reducing the evidence, not the risk.
panelPlan: The Veil Market back room works as a route exchange: runners, beacon codes, bribe lists, cargo seals, and crowded authorization slates surround Jex and his scribe.
The scribe reports a clean marker and Halev's demand for confirmation. Jex orders 'open,' never 'safe,' while signing the next slate.
A captain demands a bribe returned. Jex renames it a corridor fee and jokes that an accusation of theft proves the client understands the service.
Jex gives one runner the authorization and claims success in advance. When the scribe asks about failure, he says they have never met.
The scribe points to twelve documents bearing Jex's stamp. Jex tells them to lose eleven as runners depart in opposite directions and the corridor continues through his room.

summary: The corridor's first anomaly appears and everyone has to resist shooting at a ghost.
settingText: GREEN CORRIDOR — MARKERS ONE AND TWO

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Mark Two— what the hell is that?

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Second contact. Same mass. Same registry.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second
dialogueInline.text: Both of them answer the beacon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Nobody fire. If we don't know what it is, we don't kill it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Then we move with them. Hold the lane.

directionInline: The crossing appears stable until a second freighter resolves beside the lead with identical mass, registry, and beacon response. Naomi's first instinct is confusion; her second forces the impossibility into operational facts while multiple escorts begin targeting. Naomi cannot identify the real ship, so she changes the rule from threat response to epistemic restraint: uncertainty is not permission to fire. Ashfang's lock breaks. Both contacts continue, and Naomi chooses to escort the impossible pair rather than solve them with weapons.
panelPlan: Naomi calls Mark One clear as the lead freighter enters Mark Two and the convoy finally seems routine.
An identical freighter resolves beside it. Naomi stops mid-call; her second reports matching mass, registry, and beacon response.
Across opposing cockpits, fingers approach triggers and Ashfang paints the duplicate. Naomi orders safeties on and tells Billie to break lock.
No answer comes. Naomi states the decisive rule: if they do not know what it is, they do not kill it. The targeting lock falls away.
Wide: real and ghost freighters advance together. Naomi orders the escorts to move with both and hold the lane, turning terror into continued passage.

summary: Venn registers a tiny victory in operational language while a junior officer sees what it cost her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Gone at the boundary. No discharge, no debris.

dialogueInline.speaker: Officer
dialogueInline.text: Still answering. Still itself, as far as we can tell.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: That will have to be enough.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Log the crossing. Keep the lane open.

directionInline: The final freighter crosses and the ghost vanishes without explanation. Venn refuses to count the outcome until she confirms the real ship remains intact. Her junior officer says 'we' did it; Venn corrects the ownership because the civilians and escorts bore the passage. The officer notices Venn steadying herself against the console, but neither names the cost. Venn converts relief into policy by keeping the lane open for an unknown next arrival.
panelPlan: The last cargo icon crosses the boundary; beside it, the duplicate disappears without discharge or debris.
The officer reports clearance. Venn asks first about the duplicate, then the original freighter, refusing victory until the civilian ship answers.
The officer says, 'We did it.' Venn quietly corrects: 'They crossed.' Close on two fingers steadying against the console edge.
The officer notices; Venn catches the look and removes her hand. She orders the crossing logged and the lane kept open.
Asked whether she means the next convoy, Venn answers, 'For whoever arrives first,' as a fresh empty route extends across the display.

summary: Halev sees cargo icons as the concrete lives they will change.

dialogueInline.speaker: Medic
dialogueInline.text: Governor, clinic asked for all three antibiotic cases.

dialogueInline.speaker: Medic
dialogueInline.text: Two won't clear the waiting list.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Third case goes east. Their fever ward has been reusing filters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Medic
dialogueInline.text: North Ring is asking for batteries too.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: North gets heaters. Batteries stay on the dock pumps.

dialogueInline.speaker: Medic
dialogueInline.text: They're going to say you chose machinery over people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: If the pumps stop, they can say it underwater.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Heaters to North Ring. Two antibiotic cases to the clinic, one east. Batteries stay here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Halev
dialogueInline.text: Keep unloading. Then we find out what we still don't have.

directionInline: The cargo arrives as competing human claims, not a victory tableau. A medic asks Halev to send all antibiotics to one visible waiting list. Halev knows an unseen fever ward needs one case and that the dock pumps must keep the settlement alive. He accepts that every allocation will look cruel from somewhere else, then divides the actual crates. When distant windows light, he does not celebrate; he asks what the corridor failed to bring.
panelPlan: Freighters unload into Auric's crowded working port as clerks, carts, and repair crews lose control of the flow. A medic intercepts Halev beside three antibiotic cases.
The medic demands all three for the clinic. Halev assigns one east to a fever ward that has been reusing filters, making the shortage personal on both sides.
North Ring also wants batteries. Halev reserves them for failing dock pumps; the medic warns how the choice will sound, and Halev answers with the consequence of stopping the pumps.
Halev directs heaters, antibiotics, and batteries into separate carts. Workers split the loads immediately.
Apartment windows begin to light in the distance. Asked about the next load, Halev orders unloading to continue so they can discover what is still missing.

summary: Abby admits why she let the convoy pass; Tessa offers a different future without demanding an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: I stopped her wasting our next clinic.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: That the clinic you're counting twice?

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: One column is stock. One is casualties.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then don't make it something else.

dialogueInline.speaker: Tess
dialogueInline.text: You put your ship in front of hers.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: And she stopped. Useful thing to know.

directionInline: Abby updates clinic stock beside the casualty count, trying to make her decision look like logistics. Tess sees both columns and refuses the disguise without openly accusing her of compassion. Abby insists that stopping Billie was useful command information, not a moral choice. Tess's neutral agreement carries the implication Abby fears. Abby tells her not to name it; Tess leaves open the possibility that Abby may someday need to name it herself.
panelPlan: Abby works alone at a board where clinic stock and casualties occupy adjacent columns beside the green route.
Tess enters and says Abby stopped Billie. Abby calls it protection of their next clinic; Tess points to the two clinic columns.
Abby distinguishes stock from casualties and warns Tess not to make the act into something else. Tess notes that Abby put her own ship in front of Billie's.
Abby reduces the event to useful knowledge: Billie stopped. Tess says 'Sure'; Abby turns at last and says, 'Don't.'
Tess says she did not name anything. Abby says Tess never needs to; Tess answers, 'No. But you might,' and leaves Abby facing both columns.

summary: Naomi and Venn acknowledge each other's contribution with restrained professional warmth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Last hull is inside Auric control.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: Good. I'd hate to lose one after all that paperwork.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: The Fleet would require a form.

dialogueInline.speaker: Naomi
dialogueInline.text: With a cruiser blocking half the sky.

dialogueInline.speaker: Venn
dialogueInline.text: Send the window. We'll be there.

directionInline: Naomi confirms the last hull and tests whether Venn will claim the operation. Their shared count becomes a small joke about Fleet paperwork, allowing warmth without sentimentality. Naomi thanks Venn for protection; Venn returns agency to the Verge pilots. Naomi refuses the false modesty entirely and converts gratitude into a request for tomorrow. Venn accepts, making their professional respect an ongoing method rather than a closing compliment.
panelPlan: Naomi watches the last freighter enter Auric control and opens the channel; Venn confirms Thunderbreak has the same count.
Naomi jokes about losing a ship to paperwork. Venn unexpectedly answers that the Fleet would require a form, letting both women release a fraction of the tension.
Naomi thanks Venn for the shadow. Venn says Naomi brought them through; Naomi gestures at the cruiser that blocked half the sky.
Venn calls Thunderbreak a navigational inconvenience. Naomi asks her to be inconvenient tomorrow.
Wide: Verge ships head for Auric while Thunderbreak remains outside the lane. Venn asks for the next window and promises, 'We'll be there.'

summary: Billie's restraint holds only because Abby has temporarily imposed it; her threat becomes personal and tactical.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Convoy's gone. So is your excuse.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: I don't need an excuse to talk to you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: You brought guns to a conversation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You notice me better this way.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: Next time, I choose the mark.

dialogueInline.speaker: Abby
dialogueInline.text: Then choose one you can reach.

dialogueInline.speaker: Billie
dialogueInline.text: You think I can't reach you?

directionInline: After the convoy clears, Billie turns Ashfang nose-to-nose with Abby's smaller skiff to recover the dominance she lost. Abby refuses to move and names the humiliating fact: Billie stopped. Billie minimizes it as a single exception, but Abby treats one act of obedience as precedent. Billie makes the next target personal. Abby answers by challenging Billie's capacity to act, then lets the continued conversation prove her restraint is still holding. Billie peels away first.
panelPlan: Ashfang turns across the empty green markers and settles nose-to-nose with Abby's smaller skiff. Billie orders her to move; Abby refuses.
Billie says she needs no excuse to talk. Abby notes the guns; Billie calls them the best way to be noticed.
Abby says she noticed Billie stop. Billie insists it happened once; Abby answers, 'Once is how it starts.'
Billie threatens to choose the next mark. Abby tells her to choose one she can reach, turning the threat toward their dangerous proximity.
Billie asks whether Abby thinks she is unreachable. Abby points out Billie is still talking. Billie peels away first; Abby remains in place.

summary: Jex recognizes that a temporary compromise has made him structurally necessary and intends to own that dependency.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Six captains, nine merchants, two clinics, and people who won't say what they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Halev says your authority is temporary.

dialogueInline.speaker: Scribe
dialogueInline.text: Do I tell them the road is full?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: No. Tell them the road is negotiated.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jex
dialogueInline.text: The clinic. Let everyone else watch.

directionInline: The successful crossing creates a queue larger than Jex's office can hold. His scribe inventories the demand and reminds him that Halev's arbitration grant is temporary. Jex sees that scarcity has shifted from access to adjudication: the road is open, but every use still needs negotiation. He articulates the dependency he intends to own. Then he chooses the clinic first—not privately, but where every paying client can see what kind of broker controls the road.
panelPlan: Jex's office door opens onto captains, merchants, clinic agents, and unidentified petitioners holding route slates. The scribe counts twenty-three.
The scribe inventories the competing requests and says everyone wants tomorrow's window. Jex observes that tomorrow has become ambitious.
The scribe reminds Jex his authority is temporary and asks whether to call the road full. Jex corrects the language: the road is negotiated.
Jex says, 'Now they need the road.' Asked about tomorrow, he draws the first slate toward him: 'Tomorrow they need me.'
Asked who enters first, Jex chooses the clinic and tells the scribe to let everyone else watch. The clinic agent steps in while the queue sees power and public utility become the same transaction.
